{{short description|Fictional character created by J.R.R. Tolkien}} {{good article}} {{Use British English|date=March 2022}} {{Infobox character | name = Balin | series = [[J. R. R. Tolkien|Tolkien]] | alias = Lord of [[Moria (Middle-earth)|Moria]] | race = [[Dwarf (Middle-earth)|Dwarf]] | lbl24 = Book(s) | data24 = ''[[The Hobbit]]'' (1937)
''[[The Fellowship of the Ring]]'' (1954)
''[[Unfinished Tales]]'' (1980) }} '''Balin''' is a fictional character in [[J. R. R. Tolkien]]'s world of [[Middle-earth]]. A [[Dwarf (Middle-earth)|Dwarf]], he is an important supporting character in ''[[The Hobbit]]'', and is mentioned in ''[[The Fellowship of the Ring (book)|The Fellowship of the Ring]]''. As the Fellowship travel through the underground realm of [[Moria (Middle-earth)|Moria]], they find Balin's tomb and the Dwarves' book of records, which tells how Balin founded a colony there, becoming Lord of Moria, and that the colony was overrun by [[orc]]s. Balin featured in the 1977 [[Rankin/Bass Animated Entertainment|Rankin/Bass]] [[The Hobbit (1977 film)|animated film]] of ''The Hobbit''; in Peter Jackson's 2012–2014 [[The Hobbit (film series)|live-action film series]], where he is portrayed by [[Ken Stott]] as reluctant to search for lost gold and sympathetic to Bilbo; and in the [[The Hobbit (2003 video game)|2003 video game adaptation]] where he is voiced by [[Victor Raider-Wexler]]. == Literature == {{Quote box| |quote = The Company of the Ring stood silent beside the tomb of Balin. Frodo thought of Bilbo and his long friendship with the Dwarf, and of Balin's visit to the Shire long ago. In that dusty chamber in the mountains it seemed a thousand years ago and on the other side of the world...

... in them were large iron-bound chests of wood. All had been broken and plundered; but beside the shattered lid of one there lay the remains of a book. It had been slashed and stabbed and partly burned, and it was so stained with black and other dark marks like old blood that little of it could be read...

At last Gandalf looked up. 'It seems to be a record of the fortunes of Balin's folk', he said. 'I guess that it began with their coming to Dimrill Dale nigh on thirty years ago...' |author = [[J. R. R. Tolkien]] |source = ''[[The Fellowship of the Ring]]'', "The Bridge of Khazad-Dûm" |width = 45% |align = right }} ===Early life=== Balin was born in [[Erebor]], the son of Fundin. In the year Balin turned seven, Erebor was sacked by the dragon [[Smaug]], and the Dwarves went into exile. During that period his younger brother [[Dwalin]] was born. Their father Fundin was killed in the Battle of Azanulbizar. Balin and his brother settled in the [[Blue Mountains (Middle-earth)|Blue Mountains]] with their surviving family. Balin and Dwalin were among those who set out with Thorin's father Thráin II in an attempt to return to Erebor, but they lost Thráin under the eaves of [[Mirkwood]]. After many days of fruitless searching, they returned to the Blue Mountains.{{harvnb|Tolkien|1955}}, Appendix A ===''The Hobbit''=== Balin was a member of [[Thorin Oakenshield]]'s [[List of The Hobbit characters#Thorin's company|company of Dwarves]] who travelled with [[Bilbo Baggins]] and [[Gandalf]] in the Quest of Erebor, on which the plot of ''[[The Hobbit]]'' centres. His brother Dwalin and he were the first to arrive at Bilbo's house at the beginning of ''The Hobbit''. He played a [[viol]]. He was among those who had been at the Mountain before the dragon came. He had been 7 years old while Thorin had been 24 on that day, making him the second-eldest of the Dwarves in the company.{{harvnb|Tolkien|1937}}, ch. 1 "An Unexpected Party" Tolkien describes Balin as "their look-out man": he spotted Bilbo approaching the [[The Green Dragon (Middle-earth)|Green Dragon Inn]] at [[Bywater (Middle-earth)|Bywater]], saw the [[Troll (Middle-earth)|troll]]s' fire in the Trollshaws,{{harvnb|Tolkien|1937}}, ch. 2 "Roast Mutton" and was the first to see the [[Elf (Middle-earth)|elves]] in Mirkwood.{{harvnb|Tolkien|1937}}, ch. 8 "Flies and Spiders" After they escaped the [[Orc (Middle-earth)|goblins]] in the [[Misty Mountains]], Balin as look-out for the company failed to notice Bilbo (made invisible by wearing [[One Ring|his magic ring]]), and after this incident he came to respect Bilbo's abilities as a burglar.{{harvnb|Tolkien|1937}}, ch. 6 "Out of the Frying-Pan into the Fire" Balin served as the ''de facto'' spokesman for the party after the [[Thranduil|Elvenking]] imprisoned the Dwarves, as they did not at first realise that Thorin had been captured with them as well.{{harvnb|Tolkien|1937}}, ch. 9 "Barrels Out of Bond" In the course of the Quest, Balin was the Dwarf who developed the closest friendship with Bilbo. He was the only one who offered to look for Bilbo after he had gone down the secret Erebor passage.{{harvnb|Tolkien|1937}}, ch. 12 "Inside Information" Some years after the Quest, he and Gandalf visited Bilbo at [[Bag End]], where Balin told of the mountain's glory restored in the years after the Battle of the Five Armies. ===''The Lord of the Rings''=== [[File:Balin.jpg|thumb|An artist's rendition of Balin's tomb. The [[Angerthas Moria|runic inscription]] reads "Balin Son of Fundin, Lord of [[Moria (Middle-earth)|Moria]]".]] In ''[[The Fellowship of the Ring]]'', one of the Dwarves of Thorin's company, [[Glóin]] tells [[the Council of Elrond]] that Balin had left Erebor and ventured to reclaim [[Moria (Middle-earth)|Moria]] with a company of Dwarves including [[Óin, son of Gróin|Óin]] and [[Ori (Middle-earth)|Ori]] (two of his companions from the Quest of Erebor), and Flói, Frár, Lóni, and Náli. The fate of [[Moria (Middle-earth)#Balin's colony|Balin's colony]] was uncertain, as no word had come from Moria in many years. The [[Fellowship of the Ring (characters)|Fellowship]] (which included Balin's cousin, Glóin's son [[Gimli (Middle-earth)|Gimli]]) later happened upon Balin's tomb in the [[Chamber of Mazarbul]], and learnt of his fate from the Dwarves' book of records, the [[Book of Mazarbul]]. It told how Balin discovered [[Durin's Axe]], and established a small colony, but it was overrun by orcs and Balin was killed by an orc archer in Dimrill Dale. Thus he died in the same place as his father, having been self-proclaimed Lord of Moria for less than five years. Balin's tomb was inscribed "Balin Fundinul Uzbad Khazad-Dûmu", with smaller runes beneath giving the translation into English (as the representation of Tolkien’s [[fictional language|invented language]] of [[Westron]]): "Balin, son of Fundin, Lord of Moria".{{harvnb|Tolkien|1954a}}, book 2, ch. 5 "The Bridge of Khazad-dûm" ==Analysis== [[File:The_Book_of_Mazarbul,_first_page.jpg|thumb|The first page from ''[[The Book of Mazarbul]]'', a facsimile artefact created by Tolkien to support the story of Balin's death.]] The Tolkien scholar [[John D. Rateliff]] writes that Balin is the only Dwarf of Thorin's company whose name does not come directly from the [[Old Norse]] poem ''[[Völuspá]]'', part of the ''[[Poetic Edda]]''.{{cite book |last=Rateliff |first=John D. |author-link=John D. Rateliff |date=2007 |title=The History of the Hobbit: Part I. Mr. Baggins |location=Boston, New York |publisher=[[Houghton Mifflin]] |pages=23–24 |isbn=978-0-618-96847-3 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7QMLmRPUkCEC }} The name appears in Sir [[Thomas Malory]]'s [[Middle English literature|Middle English]] prose tale ''[[Le Morte d'Arthur]]'', but in Rateliff's view [[Sir Balin]] is not nearly as likeable a character. The Tolkien scholar [[Tom Shippey]] notes that in the final scene of ''The Hobbit'', Balin, Bilbo, and Gandalf discuss the connection between [[Prophecy in The Lord of the Rings|prophecy]], individual action, and truth. Balin states that the new master of [[Dale (Middle-earth)|Dale]] is wise and popular, and the people "are making songs which say that in his day the rivers run with gold."{{harvnb|Tolkien|1937}}, ch. 19 "The Last Stage" They agree that "after a fashion", the [[metaphor]]s can indeed be true, that in Shippey's words "romance and reality are differences of presentation not of fact".{{cite book |last=Shippey |first=Tom |author-link=Tom Shippey |title=[[The Road to Middle-Earth]] |date=2005 |edition=3rd |orig-year=1982 |publisher=[[HarperCollins]] |location=New York City|isbn=978-0261102750 |pages=104, 166–167}} When Balin leaves, disastrously, to seek his fortune in Moria, "a shadow of disquiet" came over the Dwarves, as [[Glóin]] reports to the [[Council of Elrond]].{{harvnb|Tolkien|1954a}}, book 2, ch. 2 "[[The Council of Elrond]]" Shippey writes that the metaphor of the shadow is ominous, and ambiguous: it could mean simple earthly discontent, or it could mean a spell from [[Mordor]]: "maybe Balin simultaneously fell [made his own choice] and was pushed [bewitched]." Tolkien expended enormous effort on constructing a [[facsimile]] ''Book of Mazarbul'' to resemble the burnt, torn volume abandoned at Balin's tomb, carefully staining and tearing the paper and burning in the burn-marks to make it as authentic as possible.{{cite encyclopedia |last=Holmes |first=John R. |editor-last=Drout |editor-first=Michael D. C. |editor-link=Michael D. C. Drout |title=Art and Illustrations by Tolkien |encyclopedia=[[J.R.R. Tolkien Encyclopedia]] |year=2013 |orig-year=2007 |publisher=[[Routledge]] |location=Abingdon, England|isbn=978-0-415-86511-1 |pages=27–32}} However, his publisher [[Allen & Unwin]] chose not to include [[Tolkien's artwork#Mazarbul|his artwork]] in the first edition, prompting Tolkien to remark that without it the text at the start of "The Bridge of Khazad-Dûm" was "rather absurd".{{harvnb|Carpenter|2023|loc=#141 to [[Allen & Unwin]], 9 October 1953 }} ==Adaptations== [[File:Balin, from the Hobbit.jpg|thumb|Ken Stott as a "visually distinctive"{{cite journal |last1=Riga |first1=Frank P. |last2=Thum |first2=Maureen |last3=Kollmann |first3=Judith |title=From Children's Book to Epic Prequel: Peter Jackson's Transformation of Tolkien's 'The Hobbit' |journal=[[Mythlore]] |date=2014 |volume=32 |issue=2 |page=Article 8 |url=https://dc.swosu.edu/mythlore/vol32/iss2/8}} Balin in [[Peter Jackson]]'s film series ''[[The Hobbit (film series)|The Hobbit]]'']] [[Don Messick]] voiced Balin in [[Rankin/Bass Animated Entertainment|Rankin/Bass]]'s [[The Hobbit (1977 film)|1977 animated version of ''The Hobbit'']].{{cite web |title=Don Messick |url=https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/Don-Messick/ |publisher=Behind the Voice Actors |access-date=4 May 2020}} In Jackson's [[The Hobbit (film series)|live-action film series of ''The Hobbit'']], Balin is portrayed by [[Ken Stott]] as reluctant to go on the quest for old gold, whether or not the dragon had stolen it from Balin's ancestors. As such, he is sympathetic to Bilbo, who appears quite unsuitable for the task he is being given.{{cite news |last=Whitaker |first=Andrew |title=Scottish independence: Ken Stott backs "Yes" |url=https://www.scotsman.com/whats-on/scottish-independence-ken-stott-backs-yes-1538577 |newspaper=[[The Scotsman]] |date=28 April 2014 |access-date=19 August 2022}}{{cite book |last=Sibley |first=Brian |author-link=Brian Sibley |title=The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey Official Movie Guide |url=https://archive.org/details/hobbitunexpected0000sibl |url-access=registration |year=2012 |publisher=[[Houghton Mifflin Harcourt]] |location=Boston, Massachusetts |isbn=978-0-547-89930-5 |pages=84–85, 134]}} In the [[The Hobbit (2003 video game)|2003 video game adaptation]] Balin is voiced by [[Victor Raider-Wexler]].{{cite web |title=Victor Raider-Wexler |url=https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/Victor-Raider-Wexler/ |website=Behind the Voice Actors |access-date=21 May 2020}} ==Family tree== {{Durin's Folk}} ==Notes== {{notelist}} ==References== ===Primary=== {{reflist|group=T|24em}} === Secondary === {{reflist|30em}} === Sources === * {{ME-ref|Letters}} * {{ME-ref|TH}} * {{ME-ref|FOTR}} * {{ME-ref|ROTK}} {{Hobbit}} {{The Lord of the Rings}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Balin (Middle-earth)}} [[Category:Middle-earth Dwarves]] [[Category:The Hobbit characters]] [[Category:The Lord of the Rings characters]] [[Category:Middle-earth rulers]] [[Category:Literary characters introduced in 1937]] [[Category:Television characters introduced in 1977]]
